text:
Nine straight games with points (7-0-2), the latest a 2-1 win over Calgary on Monday, and this run doesn't need an asterisk. Ottawa took 59% of the expected goals during it (the quality of chances), has 53% on the season, and its goals almost exactly match its chances. Linus Ullmark is 5-0-0 over his last five starts with a .935 save rate and 3.9 goals saved above expected.

At 16-6-3, the Senators sit about five points above their play by our standings model, a small cushion. The depth is the strength. Claude Giroux, Michael Amadio and Ridly Greig allow 0.88 expected goals per 60 at 5-on-5 and take 78% of the chances. Tim Stützle's line with Dylan Cozens and Fabian Zetterlund takes 65%, and Thomas Chabot and Jordan Spence have been on for 18 goals for and 8 against.

General manager Steve Staios isn't standing still. Elliotte Friedman reported Senators interest in Bryan Rust and Rickard Rakell, with Staios in Nashville on Saturday to watch the Penguins, per Coming Down the Pipe's Graeme Nichols, and The Hockey Writers has argued for moving Andre Burakovsky. The week also brought Tyler Boucher, Brian Boucher's son, to his NHL debut, and Nick Cousins back from the concussion he took on Jakob Chychrun's hit.

Our playoff odds have Ottawa at 93%, with a 31% chance at the Atlantic. What we'd watch: the backup question behind Ullmark, which the Sens Nation Podcast raised this week, and whether a scorer arrives.
headline: Ottawa's streak is real, and the GM is shopping
